hints.title: Work from the inside out
hints.body: Create a table with one row for each function. Begin with the full range of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> for real <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>, then use each row as the input interval for the next operation.
hints.recap: The domain of x is all real numbers, but each inner function has a restricted output range.
hints.pitfall: An outer sine or cosine does not necessarily receive every real input.
hints.pause: Write the first input interval and determine which trigonometric operation applies at the next row.

recall.reminder: Restrict the inner range before analysing the outer expression.

hints.title: Use the correct part of each graph
hints.body: All the inner values lie between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. These are radian values, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. Use the behaviour of sine and cosine on these short intervals.
hints.recap: Sine increases on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>; cosine increases up to zero and decreases after zero on this interval.
hints.pitfall: For cosine, checking only the endpoints misses its maximum if the input interval contains zero.
hints.pause: Map each current interval to the complete output interval, checking whether zero is included.

recall.reminder: Use trigonometric graph shape on the actual radian interval.

hints.title: Track attainment as well as bounds
hints.body: Continue the interval table through the fifth function. At every stage, record which input value produces the upper endpoint and whether that value lies in the interval supplied by the preceding row.
hints.recap: A maximum must be both an upper bound and an attained value.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume that the value producing one function maximum also produces the next function maximum.
hints.pause: Finish the range table, extract the five maxima and compare them with the listed statements.

recall.reminder: Establish the relevant intervals before comparing transformed values.

solution:
Put s=sin1, so 0<s<1. The ranges of f1 and f2 are [−1,1] and [−s,s] respectively, giving m1=1 and m2=s.

Cosine maps [−s,s] onto [coss,1], so m3=1. Sine is increasing throughout that positive interval, so the range of f4 is [sin(coss),s] and m4=s.

The last interval is wholly inside (0,1). Cosine is decreasing there, so f5 has range [coss,cos(sin(coss))]. In particular 0<m5<1. These interval endpoints are all attained.

Thus m1=m3=1, 0<m2=m4<1, and 0<m5<1. Answer: E.
knowledgePattern: Propagate complete ranges through nested trigonometric functions
